audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer rows read 'Skill' while content and packet both give Malzahar 1-3 and 6, even at 4-5, Ekko at both item stages.
audit.why: Ekko's Q is 1075 range but his engage is a 325-range Phase Dive, so a ranged shove beats him pre-6; Chronobreak drops from 110s to 50s with ranks and items, which is what flips the lane.
audit.corrected: Sides aligned with content, Ekko rows dropped to 4/10, and both moved whys rewritten to argue his side.

audit.why: Level 6 versus first item is the real hinge, and Chronobreak's cooldown falling 110 to 50 is the mechanism.
audit.corrected: Spikes left; the chart now agrees with them.

audit.whatIsWrong: None of the four flagged interactions were on the page: Chronobreak untargetability, its healing, W stunning you out of your channel, and Phase Dive's auto reset.
audit.why: Chronobreak is flagged untargetable and heal; Nether Grasp is flagged channel/interruptible and Parallel Convergence is hard CC; Phase Dive is flagged autoReset, so the wind-up is the tell rather than the cast.
audit.corrected: All four written into breakdown.cooldowns and the trade rules, with real cooldowns attached.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit and referenced a nonexistent 'Iron Boundary'.
audit.why: Real numbers: Chronobreak 110/80/50, Parallel Convergence 22/20/18/16/14, Phase Dive 9/8.5/8/7.5/7.
audit.corrected: Written in and the fabricated name removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization never mentioned Grievous Wounds against a champion whose ultimate heals him.
audit.why: Chronobreak heals for a share of damage received in the rewind window, so anti-heal timing decides whether your burn actually sticks.
audit.corrected: winCon now names Grievous Wounds before chasing kills.

edits.before: He has to dive a spell shield, a silence, and a suppression — the math says he dies more often than you do.
edits.after: He dives a silence and a suppression, but Chronobreak undoes the kill — hold your last damage until it is spent.

edits.before: Tax his roams with permanent shove, shield-silence the dive, and Grasp the over-commit. Chronobreak is the clock this lane runs on — read it before every step forward.
edits.after: Tax his roams with permanent shove, silence the dash, and Grasp the over-commit. Chronobreak is the clock this lane runs on — buy Grievous Wounds before you chase kills.

edits.before: Ekko wins by landing Chronobreak, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Ekko wins by setting Parallel Convergence behind you, stunning you out of the channel, and rewinding out of the punish.

edits.before: Pop-and-punish: poke his shield off with a cheap E-tick, then Q-W-E the gap before it rebuilds — full rotations only ever land on shieldless targets.
edits.after: Chip and leave: E the wave, Q when he steps up to Timewinder, and never spend your last damage while Chronobreak is up — he heals off it.

edits.before: Trading into him with YOUR shield down — you are the squishiest scaling mage in the pool the moment the purple bubble disappears.
edits.after: Dumping your full rotation into Chronobreak — he goes untargetable, rewinds, and heals off the damage you just spent.

edits.before: - Ekko Chronobreak: matchup-defining — Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. Check it before every step-up. - spell shield (Iron Boundary) is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Chronobreak (R) is 110/80/50s and turns him untargetable, so hold your last damage until he lands. - Parallel Convergence (W) is 22s at rank 1 and its stun cancels your Nether Grasp channel. - Phase Dive (E) is 9s and opens with an auto reset — the wind-up is the cue.

edits.before: Good trade: Pop-and-punish: poke his shield off with a cheap E-tick, then Q-W-E the gap before it rebuilds — full rotations only ever land on shieldless targets. Bad trade: Trading into him with YOUR shield down — you are the squishiest scaling mage in the pool the moment the purple bubble disappears.
edits.after: Good trade: chip and leave — E the wave, Q when he steps up to Timewinder, and never spend your last damage while Chronobreak is up because he heals off it. Bad trade: dumping your full rotation into Chronobreak, since he goes untargetable, rewinds, and heals off everything you just spent.

edits.before: Carry by subtraction — every fight starts 4v5 when your R lands; your job is the wave control that makes the fight happen on your timer.
edits.after: Carry by timing R around Chronobreak — with his 110-second rewind spent, one suppression on Ekko removes the only diver they have.

edits.before: Pop-and-punish: poke his shield off with a cheap E-tick, then Q-W-E the gap before it rebuilds — full rotations only ever land on shieldless targets.
edits.after: Phase Dive is only 325 range on a 9-second cooldown — hold the silence for the dash entry, not the 1075-range Timewinder you can sidestep.

edits.before: Trading into him with YOUR shield down — you are the squishiest scaling mage in the pool the moment the purple bubble disappears.
edits.after: With R spent you have no answer to Phase Dive, and Chronobreak heals him off the damage you did while taking that plate.

edits.before: Flash + Teleport standard — TP doubles your shove-tax map game. Ghost-cleanse setups exist into hard dive; Ignite pairs with R kill threats if you want lane blood.
edits.after: Flash + Teleport standard — TP turns every crashed wave into a map play. Ghost-cleanse setups exist into hard dive; Ignite pairs with R kill threats if you want lane blood.

edits.before: Liandry's spike: visions melt waves AND health bars. Suppress-into-burn kills through most defensive answers.
edits.after: His first item lands and Q-E burst plus a shorter Chronobreak escapes anything short of full lockdown.

edits.before: Late Malz is a number: one suppression on their carry equals one won teamfight. Shield up, flank smart, press R.
edits.after: Mobility and a 50-second rewind heal outlast one suppression — R becomes peel for whoever he Phase Dives.

notes: Rows 0-4 whys already argued Malzahar's side, so only the sides needed moving there; rows 5-6 whys described Malzahar winning and were rewritten in the same proposal. win[N] needed no edits — the content layer was already correct, so any win[N] edit would have been a no-op. 'Iron Boundary' in breakdown.cooldowns was a fabricated ability name and is gone. All four flagged missing interactions are now on the page.
